messages.author: afabdb12651bef78
messages.subject: Spatial random effects with car.normal
parts:
Hello,

I'm struggling with a linear model which has spatial random-effects.
In WinBUGS it runs nice.
But in nimble I'm getting this awkward message -
"Error in cc_expandDetermNodesInExpr(model, expr[[i]], targetNode, skipExpansions) :
  something went wrong with Daniel's understanding of newNimbleModel"

When I remove the structured spatial part, S[ region[i] ], everything goes ok.
A part of the code is given below.


ImputCode <- nimbleCode({

   for(i in 1:N){

   ### Men Model
        men[i] ~ dnorm(mu.men[i], prec.men)
        mu.men[i] <- beta1[1] + beta1[2]*X1[i] + beta1[3]*X2[i] + beta1[4]*X3[i] +
                           U[ region[i] ] + S[ region[i] ]
      }

      ## CAR prior distribution for spatial random effects:
      for(k in 1:sum.numneighbours) { weights[k] <- 1 }
      S[1 : n.region] ~ car.normal(adj[1:sum.numneighbours], weights[1:sum.numneighbours], numneighbours[1:n.region], tau.car)

      ## Prior for the tau.car considering an Uniforme distribution for the std
      tau.car ~ dgamma(0.5, 0.0005)

      ## normal prior for the unstructured random effects within each municipality
      for ( j in 1:n.region) {
           U[j] ~ dnorm(0, tau.U[j])           # Unstructured normal:
          }

    })

messages.subject: Re: Spatial random effects with car.normal
parts:
Awkward, indeed.

Are you able to also email the "constants" argument to nimbleModel() that you're using?  Presumably including elements "N", "sum.numneighbours", "n.region", and perhaps others?

If you would prefer not to share that "on list", then perhaps instead emailing it directly to me?  that will really help us get to the bottom of the problem here.

Thanks!

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Spatial random effects with car.normal
parts:
Rui, thanks for continuing to correspond with me about the error you were experiencing using the car.normal distribution in NIMBLE.  It was helpful to help diagnose the problem.

After looking into this, I found a minor bug in the NIMBLE's MCMC conjugacy checking system, the specific only for CAR model structure.  Specifically, the conjugacy checking of the individual components of the CAR distribution was giving a situation where the "deterministic node expansion" was resulting in the wrong expanded expression, and thus not finding the CAR node for the conjugacy check, which should always be in that expression.  In this case, your use of car.normal, or equivalently, dcar_normal, for spatial random effects distribution, was triggering the bug.

The good news, is that this bug would only cause some model structures to fail at the time of MCMC building (buildMCMC()), and would never result in an MCMC being built, or giving incorrect results.  So there's no danger of incorrect inferences.

Also, I was able to fix this bug, so that the MCMC will operate fine on these CAR models.  The fix has been added to our development branch ("devel") of NIMBLE.  Until our next release, when this will be added to the version of NIMBLE on CRAN, you can install this development version directly using the R code below. 

remove.packages('nimble')
library(devtools)
install_github('nimble-dev/nimble', ref = 'devel', subdir = 'packages/nimble')
library(nimble)

Please try this out, and let me know if this fixes the problem for your model.

Cheers, thanks for your use of NIMBLE.

Daniel
for the NIMBLE development team
